name: Gāyatrī Mantra
source: Ṛgveda 3.62.10, prefixed with ॐ and the three vyāhṛtis
devanagari:
ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः
तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं
भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि
धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात्
transliteration:
oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ
tat savitur vareṇyaṃ
bhargo devasya dhīmahi
dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt

translations.label: Translation — after S. Radhakrishnan (1953)
translations.text: We meditate on the adorable glory of the radiant sun; may She inspire our intelligence.

word_meanings.meaning: of Savitṛ, the impelling sun (genitive of savitṛ)
most excellent, to be chosen, desirable
may we meditate on, may we hold (1st person plural middle)

notes: ॐ and भूर्भुवः स्वः are the mahāvyāhṛti prefix — the three worlds — added in later ritual use; the three lines after it are the Ṛgvedic verse proper, addressed to Savitṛ in the gāyatrī metre the mantra is named for (three octosyllabic lines). Also called the Sāvitrī mantra. In the last line धियः + यः shows visarga sandhi: -aḥ → -o before a voiced sound, giving धियो यो. The verse's own grammar is masculine — यः and प्रचोदयात् refer back to सवितुः देवस्य — so translations render it "he"; the feminine "She" above follows the later devotional identification of the mantra with the goddess Gāyatrī, Veda-mātā, the Mother of the Vedas.

audio_source.credit: Shri Rattan Mohan Sharma, via the Internet Archive

name: Prātaḥ Smaraṇa Stotram
source: Attributed to Ādi Śaṅkara; three verses (the closing phala-śruti verse is omitted)
devanagari:
प्रातः स्मरामि हृदि संस्फुरदात्मतत्त्वं
सच्चित्सुखं परमहंसगतिं तुरीयम्
यत्स्वप्नजागरसुषुप्तिमवैति नित्यं
तद्ब्रह्म निष्कलमहं न च भूतसङ्घः

प्रातर्भजामि मनसा वचसामगम्यं
वाचो विभान्ति निखिला यदनुग्रहेण
यन्नेतिनेतिवचनैर्निगमा अवोचं
स्तं देवदेवमजमच्युतमाहुरग्र्यम्

प्रातर्नमामि तमसः परमर्कवर्णं
पूर्णं सनातनपदं पुरुषोत्तमाख्यम्
यस्मिन्निदं जगदशेषमशेषमूर्तौ
रज्ज्वां भुजङ्गम इव प्रतिभासितं वै
transliteration:
prātaḥ smarāmi hṛdi saṃsphurad ātma tattvaṃ
sac cit sukhaṃ parama haṃsa gatiṃ turīyam
yat svapna jāgara suṣuptim avaiti nityaṃ
tad brahma niṣkalam ahaṃ na ca bhūta saṅghaḥ

prātar bhajāmi manasā vacasām agamyaṃ
vāco vibhānti nikhilā yad anugraheṇa
yan neti neti vacanair nigamā avocaṃ
s taṃ deva devam ajam acyutam āhur agryam

prātar namāmi tamasaḥ param arka varṇaṃ
pūrṇaṃ sanātana padaṃ puruṣottamākhyam
yasminn idaṃ jagad aśeṣam aśeṣa mūrtau
rajjvāṃ bhujaṅgama iva pratibhāsitaṃ vai

translations.label: Translation — Swami Tadatmananda (Arsha Bodha)
translations.text:
At dawn, I meditate on the reality shining in my heart,
sat chit ananda, sought by saints, transcendent,
which forever abides in waking, dreams, and sleep.
I am that indivisible brahman, not this material body.

At dawn, I worship him beyond words and thoughts,
who causes all words and thoughts to arise,
declared as "not this, not this" in the scriptures,
the unborn, immutable, primal, god of gods.

At dawn, I bow to him shining through the darkness,
the limitless, eternal abode, the supreme person,
in whom the entire world appears
like a snake appears on a rope.

notes: The pada break in verse 2 falls mid-sandhi: ...निगमा अवोचं / स्तं देवदेवम्... reads continuously as nigamā avocaṃs taṃ devadevam ("the scriptures declared him... the god of gods") — स्/स is the start of तम् carried onto the next printed line, a common effect of the meter not aligning with word boundaries. A fourth, phala-śruti verse (‘whoever recites this at dawn attains the supreme state’) traditionally follows but is not carded here, the deck being about the meditation itself rather than the fruit of reciting it.
